stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: Sweep the amplitude $A$, period $T$, and celerity $c$ sliders. Notice how the spatial wavelength $\lambda$ visible along the rope depends on both $c$ and $T$. Advance when each slider has swept at least half of its range.
stages.concept: For a sinusoidal traveling wave $y(x,t) = A\,\sin(\omega t - k x)$, the spatial period is the wavelength $\lambda = c \cdot T = c / f$. $A$ sets the height of the crests, $T$ sets how long one full oscillation lasts, and $c$ sets how fast the pattern moves along the rope.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: A target wavelength $\lambda^*$ is bracketed on the rope. Adjust $c$ and $T$ so that the visible spatial wavelength matches the bracket. Many pairs $(c, T)$ satisfy $c \cdot T = \lambda^*$.
stages.concept: Feature match: $\lambda = c \cdot T$. If you fix $T$, then $c = \lambda^* / T$. If you fix $c$, then $T = \lambda^* / c$. The amplitude $A$ does not affect $\lambda$.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The wave rendering is hidden. Two points $M_A$ and $M_B$ marked on the rope must oscillate in phase, and they are exactly one wavelength apart: $\Delta x = \lambda$. Compute $(c, T)$ on paper so that $c \cdot T = \Delta x$, then set the sliders and submit.
stages.concept: Two points on the rope oscillate in phase iff their separation is an integer multiple of the wavelength: $\Delta x = n \lambda$ with $n \in \mathbb{N}$. Here $n = 1$, so $\lambda = \Delta x$ and any pair $(c, T)$ with $c \cdot T = \Delta x$ is a valid answer.

labels.tip1: sweep A, T, c to see how each shapes the wave
labels.tip2: align the visible spatial wavelength with the bracket Δx = λ*
labels.tip3: compute c · T = Δx on paper, then set the sliders
labels.peek_tip_formula: Rearrange: λ = c · T → T = λ / c. Pick any c, then compute T.
labels.peek_tip_anchor: Order of magnitude: at c = 2 m/s, T = λ/2 seconds. Adjust from there.

1.1: Which slider changes the amplitude of the wave? Which one changes its wavelength?
1.2: Fix c and sweep T. The spatial wavelength scales linearly with T: doubling T doubles λ.
1.3: The core relationship is λ = c · T. Sweep c and T independently and watch λ track their product.

2.1: Read the target bracket Δx = λ* on the rope. Which product of your sliders must equal this length?
2.2: Fix one of c or T at a round value, then solve the other from c · T = λ*.
2.3: For λ* = 1.5 m, one direct choice is c = 3 m/s and T = 0.5 s (3 × 0.5 = 1.5).

3.1: The two markers M_A and M_B are exactly one wavelength apart. What does that tell you about λ?
3.2: Substitute λ = Δx into λ = c · T. That is one equation with two unknowns — you get to pick one of them.
3.3: Pick a convenient c (say, 2 m/s), then T = Δx / c. Set both sliders and submit.
